selected_evidence.requirement: Disable core dumps for local service accounts
selected_evidence.summary: Shows the persistent manager configuration, effective default limit, post-reboot inherited zero limit, zero generated payload files, and zero soft/hard limits for every running local service-account process.
Controlled crashes retained PID, UID, signal, and unit metadata in the journal while explicitly reporting that no coredump was generated.
Captures the healthy baseline, acknowledged native reboot schedule, changed boot identity, recovered services and retained journal data, persisted policy, running system state, and zero failed units.

commands.stdout:
--- coredump manual excerpt ---
\fIStorage=\fR
.RS 4
Controls where to store cores\&. One of
"none",
"external", and
"journal"\&. When
"none", the core dumps may be logged (including the backtrace if possible), but not stored permanently\&. When
"external"
(the default), cores will be stored in
/var/lib/systemd/coredump/\&. When
"journal", cores will be stored in the journal and rotated following normal journal rotation patterns\&.
.sp
When cores are stored in the journal, they might be compressed following journal compression settings, see
\fBjournald.conf\fR(5)\&. When cores are stored externally, they will be compressed by default, see below\&.
.sp
Note that in order to process a coredump (i\&.e\&. extract a stack trace) the core must be written to disk first\&. Thus, unless
\fIProcessSizeMax=\fR
is set to 0 (see below), the core will be written to
/var/lib/systemd/coredump/
either way (under a temporary filename, or even in an unlinked file),
\fIStorage=\fR
thus only controls whether to leave it there even after it was processed\&.
.sp
Added in version 215\&.
.RE
.PP
\fICompress=\fR
.RS 4
Controls compression for external storage\&. Takes a boolean argument, which defaults to
"yes"\&.
.sp
Added in version 215\&.
.RE
.PP
\fIProcessSizeMax=\fR
.RS 4
The maximum size in bytes of a core which will be processed\&. Core dumps exceeding this size may be stored, but the stack trace will not be generated\&. Like other sizes in this same config file, the usual suffixes to the base of 1024 are allowed (B, K, M, G, T, P, and E)\&. Defaults to 1G on 32\-bit systems, 32G on 64\-bit systems\&.
.sp
Setting
\fIStorage=none\fR
and
\fIProcessSizeMax=0\fR
disables all coredump handling except for a log entry\&.
.sp
Added in version 215\&.
.RE
.PP
\fIEnterNamespace=\fR
.RS 4
For processes belonging to a PID namespace, controls whether
\fBsystemd-coredump\fR(8)
shall attempt to process core dumps on the host, using debug information from the file system hierarchy (i\&.e\&. the mount namespace) of the process that crashed\&. Access
...[TRUNCATED 1429 CHARACTERS]...
edump to be saved in separate files on disk (default: 1G on 32\-bit systems, 32G on 64\-bit systems) or in the journal (default: 767M)\&. Note that the journal service enforces a hard limit on journal log records of 767M, and will ignore larger submitted log records\&. Hence,
\fIJournalSizeMax=\fR
may be lowered relative to the default, but not increased\&. Unit suffixes are allowed just as in
\fBProcessSizeMax=\fR\&.
.sp
\fIExternalSizeMax=infinity\fR
sets the core size to unlimited\&.
.sp
Added in version 215\&.
.RE
.PP
\fIMaxUse=\fR, \fIKeepFree=\fR
--- service manager manual references ---
.sp
Added in version 228\&.
.RE
.PP
\fIDefaultLimitCPU=\fR, \fIDefaultLimitFSIZE=\fR, \fIDefaultLimitDATA=\fR, \fIDefaultLimitSTACK=\fR, \fIDefaultLimitCORE=\fR, \fIDefaultLimitRSS=\fR, \fIDefaultLimitNOFILE=\fR, \fIDefaultLimitAS=\fR, \fIDefaultLimitNPROC=\fR, \fIDefaultLimitMEMLOCK=\fR, \fIDefaultLimitLOCKS=\fR, \fIDefaultLimitSIGPENDING=\fR, \fIDefaultLimitMSGQUEUE=\fR, \fIDefaultLimitNICE=\fR, \fIDefaultLimitRTPRIO=\fR, \fIDefaultLimitRTTIME=\fR
.RS 4
These settings control various default resource limits for processes executed by units\&. See
\fBsetrlimit\fR(2)
for details\&. These settings may be overridden in individual units using the corresponding
\fILimitXXX=\fR
directives and they accept the same parameter syntax, see
\fBsystemd.exec\fR(5)
for details\&. Note that these resource limits are only defaults for units, they are not applied to the service manager process (i\&.e\&. PID 1) itself\&.
.sp
Most of these settings are unset, which means the resource limits are inherited from the kernel or, if invoked in a container, from the container manager\&. However, the following have defaults:
.sp
.RS 4
.ie n \{\
\h'-04'\(bu\h'+03'\c
.\}
.el \{\
.sp -1
.IP \(bu 2.3
.\}
\fIDefaultLimitNOFILE=\fR
defaults to 1024:524288\&.
.RE
.sp
.RS 4
.ie n \{\
\h'-04'\(bu\h'+03'\c
.\}
.el \{\

commands.command:
set -u
probe=[REDACTED].service
start=$(date +%s)
systemctl reset-failed "$probe" 2>/dev/null || true
systemd-run --quiet --unit="$probe" --uid=systemd-resolve --property=StandardOutput=journal /usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os,resource,signal; print("postreboot-probe uid=%d core_limit=%s" % (os.getuid(),resource.getrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CORE)),flush=True); os.kill(os.getpid(),signal.SIGSEGV)'
i=0
while [ "$i" -lt 20 ]; do state=$(systemctl show "$probe" -p ActiveState --value 2>/dev/null || true); [ "$state" != active ] && [ "$state" != activating ] && break; sleep 0.25; i=$((i+1)); done
sleep 1
printf '%s\n' '--- post-reboot inherited policy and result ---'
systemctl show "$probe" -p User -p LimitCORE -p ExecMainCode -p ExecMainStatus -p Result -p ActiveState --no-pager
printf '%s\n' '--- post-reboot normal crash log ---'
journalctl --since="@$start" -u "$probe" --no-pager -o short-monotonic
printf '%s\n' '--- post-reboot coredump metadata ---'
journalctl --since="@$start" COREDUMP_UNIT="$probe" --no-pager -o verbose | sed -n '/MESSAGE=/p;/COREDUMP_PID=/p;/COREDUMP_UID=/p;/COREDUMP_UNIT=/p;/COREDUMP_SIGNAL=/p;/COREDUMP_FILENAME=/p'
newcores=$(find /var/lib/systemd/coredump -maxdepth 1 -type f -newermt "@$start" -print 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
printf 'new_external_core_payload_files=%s\n' "$newcores"
[ "$newcores" -eq 0 ]
systemctl reset-failed "$probe" 2>/dev/null || true

commands.command:
set -eu
printf 'boot_id='; cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
printf 'system_state='; systemctl is-system-running
printf 'failed_units='; systemctl --failed --no-legend --plain | wc -l
printf 'journald='; systemctl is-active systemd-journald.service
printf 'coredump_socket='; systemctl is-active systemd-coredump.socket
printf 'manager_default_core='; systemctl show --property=DefaultLimitCORE --value
printf 'core_pattern='; cat /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern
uid_min=$(awk '$1=="UID_MIN" {print $2}' /etc/login.defs); [ -n "$uid_min" ] || uid_min=1000
printf '%s\n' '--- running processes owned by local service accounts ---'
found=0
for unit in $(systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running --no-legend --plain | awk '{print $1}'); do
  pid=$(systemctl show "$unit" -p MainPID --value)
  [ "$pid" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null || continue
  uid=$(awk '/^Uid:/ {print $2}' "/proc/$pid/status")
  if [ "$uid" -gt 0 ] && [ "$uid" -lt "$uid_min" ]; then
    name=$(getent passwd "$uid" | cut -d: -f1)
    limit=$(awk '/^Max core file size/ {print "soft=" $(NF-2) " hard=" $(NF-1) " unit=" $NF}' "/proc/$pid/limits")
    printf '%s account=%s uid=%s pid=%s %s\n' "$unit" "$name" "$uid" "$pid" "$limit"
    [ "$(awk '/^Max core file size/ {print $(NF-1)}' "/proc/$pid/limits")" = 0 ]
    found=$((found+1))
  fi
done
printf 'audited_local_service_processes=%s\n' "$found"
[ "$found" -gt 0 ]
printf '%s\n' '--- latest post-reboot crash record ---'
journalctl COREDUMP_UNIT=[REDACTED].service -n 1 --no-pager -o short-iso
